name: Proxy
intent: Put a stand-in object in front of another to control access: delay its creation, cache results, check permissions or log calls.
scenario: A photo gallery shows images. Loading a photo from disk is slow, so a proxy loads each one only when it is first displayed, and reuses it afterwards.
problem: Creating a RealImage loads the file immediately. A gallery with 100 photos loads all 100 at startup, even though the user looks at three. Startup is slow and memory is wasted.
solution: Create an ImageProxy with the same interface as the real image. It stores only the filename. On the first display() it creates the RealImage, then delegates. Later calls reuse the loaded image. The gallery cannot tell the difference.
pain: All images load at startup, used or not
Startup time grows with the size of the gallery
The gallery code is tangled with loading concerns
benefits: Opening the gallery is instant: only proxies are created
A photo loads on first view, once
The gallery uses the same Image interface for both
Lazy loading is isolated in one class
whenToUse: Lazy initialisation of expensive objects (virtual proxy)
Access control or permission checks (protection proxy)
Caching, logging, or talking to a remote object as if it were local
whenNotToUse: The object is cheap or always needed
Extra indirection would hide an important cost from callers
A simple cache or lazy variable would do the same job
pitfalls: Latency moves to the first use, which can surprise users
A proxy that does too much becomes hard to reason about
Must keep the same interface, or clients can tell it apart
Easy to confuse with Decorator: a proxy controls access, a decorator adds behaviour

roles.label: Subject
roles.description: The interface shared by the real object and its proxy.

roles.label: Proxy
roles.description: Same interface; controls access and creates the real object when needed.

roles.label: Client
roles.description: Uses the subject interface and never knows which one it holds.
